fields.label: Sign in with
fields.hint: Your national identity provider. CREST never sees a credential of yours.

callouts.title: Why this screen exists
callouts.text: One door, every console role. What you see after signing in is decided by the roles you hold — never by which link you opened.

callouts.title: What this screen never does
callouts.text: It never asks which role you want, and never offers a role you do not hold. A role is granted in the registry and read back here — picking your own would make authority a matter of self-declaration.

forbidden.why: n1 never asks which role you want — a self-declared role would make authority self-declaration

n2.title: Where do you want to work?
n2.appbar: CREST Console Peter Otieno · signed in

callouts.title: What this screen never does
callouts.text: It never lists a context you hold no role in, and never shows a project before somebody handed it to you. An empty list is a true answer: it means a role still has to be granted.

n3.title: One rail, two actors
n3.appbar: CREST Console Peter Otieno · Org Admin

callouts.title: The rule this screen sets
callouts.text: An entry is never hidden because of your role. A row you cannot act on stays visible and names who can — a missing row reads as a feature that does not exist, which is a lie the console can avoid telling.

callouts.title: What the reference already decided
callouts.text: The rail is identical for both J3 actors within a section, and the reference draws three sections: the five-entry setup rail, a dashboard rail, and a finance and support rail. Only the appbar identity changes between the two actors.

n4.title: Ministry of Health handed you a project
n4.appbar: CREST Console Dr. Alice Mutua · Project Configurator

fields.label: What is still yours to answer

callouts.title: Why handing it back is a real button
callouts.text: A named owner who never agreed is worse than no owner: the project looks staffed and is not. Declining records who declined and why, and returns the project to the Org Admin's queue rather than deleting anything.

n5.title: People & roles is not yours to change
n5.appbar: CREST Console Dr. Alice Mutua · Project Configurator

fields.label: What you can see here, read only

callouts.title: The rule this screen sets
callouts.text: No blank refusal, and no vanished entry. A guard states the role you would need, names somebody who can grant it, and still shows whatever you are allowed to read.

forbidden.why: n5 states a boundary in words and names who can grant the role; an HTTP status code shown to a user is the blank refusal this screen exists to replace
same rule as 403 — no raw status vocabulary on a guard screen
